title: 连续尺寸多米诺装入正方形

knownBest.source: The largest domino, 1 × 2, needs a square of side 2 on its own: a square holds the projections of what it contains on both of its sides, and turned through θ (0 ≤ θ ≤ 90°, the rest by symmetry) the domino projects to lengths 1 sin θ + 2 cos θ and 1 cos θ + 2 sin θ. The first is at least 2 exactly when tan(θ/2) ≤ 1/2 (θ ≤ 53.13°), the second exactly when θ ≥ 36.87°, so one of them always is. The square of side 2 holds all 1 pieces: 1 × 2 lying in [0, 2] × [0, 1]. So s = 2 is optimal (Friedman's table marks it Trivial).

The largest domino, 2 × 4, needs a square of side 4 on its own: a square holds the projections of what it contains on both of its sides, and turned through θ (0 ≤ θ ≤ 90°, the rest by symmetry) the domino projects to lengths 2 sin θ + 4 cos θ and 2 cos θ + 4 sin θ. The first is at least 4 exactly when tan(θ/2) ≤ 1/2 (θ ≤ 53.13°), the second exactly when θ ≥ 36.87°, so one of them always is. The square of side 4 holds all 2 pieces: 2 × 4 standing in [0, 2] × [0, 4], 1 × 2 standing in [2, 3] × [0, 2]. So s = 4 is optimal (Friedman's table marks it Trivial).

The largest domino, 3 × 6, needs a square of side 6 on its own: a square holds the projections of what it contains on both of its sides, and turned through θ (0 ≤ θ ≤ 90°, the rest by symmetry) the domino projects to lengths 3 sin θ + 6 cos θ and 3 cos θ + 6 sin θ. The first is at least 6 exactly when tan(θ/2) ≤ 1/2 (θ ≤ 53.13°), the second exactly when θ ≥ 36.87°, so one of them always is. The square of side 6 holds all 3 pieces: 3 × 6 standing in [0, 3] × [0, 6], 2 × 4 standing in [3, 5] × [0, 4], 1 × 2 standing in [5, 6] × [0, 2]. So s = 6 is optimal (Friedman's table marks it Trivial).

The largest domino, 4 × 8, needs a square of side 8 on its own: a square holds the projections of what it contains on both of its sides, and turned through θ (0 ≤ θ ≤ 90°, the rest by symmetry) the domino projects to lengths 4 sin θ + 8 cos θ and 4 cos θ + 8 sin θ. The first is at least 8 exactly when tan(θ/2) ≤ 1/2 (θ ≤ 53.13°), the second exactly when θ ≥ 36.87°, so one of them always is. The square of side 8 holds all 4 pieces: 4 × 8 standing in [0, 4] × [0, 8], 3 × 6 standing in [4, 7] × [0, 6], 2 × 4 lying in [4, 8] × [6, 8], 1 × 2 standing in [7, 8] × [0, 2]. So s = 8 is optimal (Friedman's table marks it Trivial).
